Needs Android 11 or newer. Glashutte activates a shell-uid helper through Wireless Debugging, an Android 11+ feature.

1. Make sure the phone is on Wi-Fi (Wireless debugging needs it).\n2. Settings > Developer options > turn Wireless debugging ON. If Developer options is missing: Settings > About phone > tap “Build number” seven times.\n3. Come back to Glashutte; it reconnects by itself.
Pair here instead (type the code in this app)

Use this if the notification does not appear or pairing keeps failing. Put Settings and Glashutte side by side in split-screen so the “Pair device with a pairing code” dialog stays open, then type the 6-digit code and the “IP address & Port” shown in that dialog (for example 192.168.1.23:37123) and tap Pair.
After pairing, if Glashutte cannot find the connect port by itself, type the “IP address & Port” shown on the main Wireless debugging screen (a different port from the pairing one) and tap Connect.
Open Diagnostics (shows why the helper is not connected)
Until this is done, nothing can be sent into apps on the glasses: the trackpad is hidden and the mouse and keyboard do nothing.
Notifications are switched off for Glashutte, so the pairing prompt cannot appear. Turn them on in Settings, or use “Pair here instead” below.

One-time pairing, about a minute:
1. Phone on Wi-Fi. Settings > Developer options > Wireless debugging ON.
2. Tap “Pair device with a pairing code”. Leave that dialog open.
3. Pull the notification shade down over the dialog, tap “Pair” in Glashutte's notification and type the 6-digit code.
No USB cable or computer is needed. If no notification appears, or it fails, use “Pair here instead” below.

Pairing failed — check the code and that the “Pair device” dialog is still open, then try again.
Lets you enter the wireless-debugging pairing code from the notification shade.
Type the 6-digit code from the Wireless Debugging pair dialog. Pull this shade down over the dialog and answer here — Glashutte pairs while the dialog is still in front.
Connect your VITURE glasses or an external monitor to start.
Glasses connected — tap apps to add screens (up to 3).
Lets Glashutte open the phone keyboard when you tap into a text field on the glasses, so you can type from the phone.
Turn on the Glashutte accessibility service so the phone keyboard opens automatically when you tap a text field in an app on the glasses.
